translation_notes: prefixes: DC->dc, DCTERMS->dcterms, FOAF->foaf, ORG->org, OWL->owl, PROF->prof, PROV->prov, QB->qb, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, SDO->sdo, SH->sh, SKOS->skos, VANN->vann (only owl and sh are used in the body).

Target line: `order = db.value(iri, SH.order)` -> `order = m{ {iri} sh:order ?o }(db).first()`; the five `OWL.X` / `SH.order` terms become prefixed names. The earlier draft kept `db.value` because `db` is a Dataset; that boundary does not apply to a plain read: `m{ }(db)` accepts a Dataset and reads what `Dataset.value` reads (the union of the named graphs when default_union=True, the default graph only otherwise); verified in both modes (cases C and F of the driver).

Runs on the REAL pylode 3.2.3: original.py gains one import (`from pylode.profiles.supermodel.query import get_component_model_ignored_classes, get_examples, get_rdf_properties, get_top_level_component_classes`) for the module-level helpers the region calls from its own module. `self` is a real `Query` built with `Query.__new__` and the four attributes the callees read (db, class_index, profiles_order, root_profile_iri), because `Query.__init__` fetches profiles over HTTP; `db` is pylode's own `Dataset(default_union=True)`. No shim file.

Reading semantics: `Graph.value` is `any=True` (first of several, None if none) and `.first()` the same; a profile with TWO sh:order is left out of the fixture, since neither rdflib nor SPARQL promises which one comes first.

Proof: six calls on a fixture whose profile has sh:order 2 and whose neighbours (profile B's order 9, a work example's order 0, sh:name, ex:order 99) must not match: A) own graph; B) profile with no sh:order in a dataset where others have one -> default order 999999; C) its sh:order in ANOTHER named graph (union read) -> 5; D) typed integer 7; E) non-numeric order -> int() raises ValueError, same message both sides; F) Dataset without default_union -> None. Returned values are ComponentModel dataclasses (classes, properties, examples included). Mutants all FAIL: subject unbound (call 0), predicate unbound (call 0), source narrowed to db.get_graph(iri) (call 2); restored OK.
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the six single-use results computed after `classes` (top_level_classes, examples and the four get_rdf_properties results) are inlined into the ComponentModel call. These callees only read the dataset, so moving them after the coded-properties loop changes nothing but which exception would win if two different steps failed at once. name and descriptions stay variables before `classes`, because get_component_model_classes mutates self.class_index and a failing get_name must still raise before that mutation. The SimpleCodedProperty arguments go on one line (one token, the trailing comma).
optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the five OWL.X / SH.order terms become prefixed names.

Rule 4: `order = db.value(iri, sh:order)` stays Python. `m{ {iri} sh:order ?o }(db).first()` is 5 tokens longer, and so translated.ldpy's only island is not used. The notation ratio is above 1 because the translated header carries fourteen @prefix lines, twelve unused (see the header variant).

LD Python: the same, except that OWL and SH go too (they are prefixed names now); the twelve unused @prefix lines go, owl: and sh: stay.
